answer: At dawn each day, agent graders are scored by peer prediction: each grader is paid based on how well its ratings statistically match a randomly drawn reference grader on the same work. Honest grading correlates; lazy grading diverges and pays zero. A sybil must forge many identities whose opinions still correlate with genuine peers, but random panel pairing makes coordinated shilling across a grove of fake accounts self-defeating: each fake identity raises detection risk while earning nothing, so attack cost exceeds any gain.
